segments.t: Once every last order has been plated, Lyova, Senya, and Fedya stroll back into the kitchen expecting to find Aleksandr in ruins. Seeing right through their excuses, Aleksandr strips Lyova of his rank on the spot, promotes Max to sous-chef, and invites everyone to celebrate after work.
Ага, а у него реально пальцев нет.
Да ладно, не парься, по ходу разберёшься.
И вообще, приказы начальства не обсуждаются.
Alright, let's go through it step by step in English.
'Lyova, where were you?' In Russian, the idea of 'Lev' flows naturally into 'there was' without extra filler words.
'And where were the rest of you?' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'and' before landing on 'be'.
'My stomach really started hurting.' Vika brings out the contrast between 'by' and 'me' in a few short words. Max answers right away.
Ага, а у него реально пальцев нет.
'Yeah, right, and his fingers are really missing.' The grammar packs 'yeah' and 'there is no' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'Here is how it is going to be.' In Russian, the idea of 'so' flows naturally into 'like this' without extra filler words.
'You now have a new sous-chef.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'now' and finishing on 'sous-chef'. Max answers right away.
'What is your patronymic?' Notice how Russian expresses 'how' and 'patronymic' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
'Is that clear to everyone?' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'to everyone' before landing on 'clear'.
'I do not know about this.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'I' and finishing on 'know'. Max answers right away.
Да ладно, не парься, по ходу разберёшься.
'Come on, do not sweat it, you will figure it out as you go.' Notice the reflexive suffix on the verb meaning 'to steam oneself in a bathhouse', turning the action back on the subject.
И вообще, приказы начальства не обсуждаются.
'Besides, orders from management are not up for discussion.' In Russian, the idea of 'both' flows naturally into 'are discussed' without extra filler words.
'And we will celebrate your promotion right away.' Vika addresses the listener with the informal singular 'you' alongside 'to celebrate'. Max answers right away.
'I am inviting all of you.' In Russian, the idea of 'I' flows naturally into 'everyone' without extra filler words. Alright, let's listen to all those lines again from the top.
